products.name: Creatify Max
products.tagline: Your ad teammate, from strategy to creation to launch
products.description: Max is your teammate for paid ads. Share a product URL or brief and Max makes video ads, sets up campaigns on Meta and TikTok, and watches results 24/7, flagging what to fix next. You make the calls: nothing goes live without your approval.
maker_comments: As a Paid Ads Growth Manager at Creatify, I work across Google Ads, Meta, TikTok, and other channels. A huge part of my week goes into pulling reports, comparing performance, figuring out what to test next, and turning those insights into campaigns. That’s why I’m excited to share Creatify Max today. It’s an AI teammate that connects the work we usually spread across multiple tools: creating video ads, setting up campaigns on Meta and TikTok, monitoring performance, and turning winning ads into briefs for the next creative round. For me, the most valuable part is the connection between understanding what happened and deciding what to do next . A report is useful, but being able to discuss the results, develop a new creative direction, and prepare the next campaign in the same workflow makes those insights much easier to act on. I’ve been involved since the early days, helping refine the advertising strategies behind Max. Seeing it become part of our internal workflow has been especially rewarding. It remembers our playbook, incorporates feedback, and keeps us in control— no campaign goes live without our approval. I’m excited to spend more time on strategy and creative decisions, with Max helping handle the repetitive work in between. Fellow marketers: which part of your advertising workflow would you hand over first? I’d love to hear what you’d want Max to help with. Huge congratulations to everyone on the team who helped bring Max to life! 🚀

products.name: TheBold
products.tagline: Turn execution into meetings with investors
products.description: TheBold turns startup execution into direct investor access. 🎉 Launch Fast Track (Nov 17–27): pass one AI investor-readiness interview, land in the deal flow of investors who match your startup, and unlock direct meeting access. TheBold helps founders understand investor criteria, track and verify execution and traction, practice investor-specific AI simulations, and book meetings once qualified.
maker_comments: Hey Product Hunt! 👋 I’m Julia, founder of TheBold . I’ve spent the last few years working with early-stage founders and investors, and reviewed around 1,000 startup pitches along the way. Again and again, I saw the same thing happen. An investor would say: “Interesting — come back in a few months.” But almost nobody tells the founder what exactly needs to change during those months. And even when founders do make progress, getting back in front of that investor is another problem. The email gets buried, the LinkedIn message goes unread, and the investor has already seen hundreds of other startups. At some point, I got frustrated enough to ask investors in my network a slightly unusual question: " What if you gave me a few slots in your calendar every month, and I only put startups there that actually meet your investment criteria?" To my surprise, they said yes. But they added something important: metrics aren’t enough. Metrics show what a founder has already achieved. Investors also want to understand how that founder thinks, learns, executes, and whether they’re likely to turn new capital into future results. That conversation became TheBold. 👉 How it works 1. See what unlocks investors. TheBold shows you the metrics and execution signals specific investors want to see — and which ones you’re closest to qualifying for. 2. Turn the gap into commitments. Pick a goal. Regular AI syncs turn it into focused commitments for each cycle, then track what you did, learned, changed, and achieved. 3. Build your execution track record. As you complete commitments and move your metrics, TheBold builds a verified history of your traction and execution — and checks it against investor criteria. 4. Rehearse the investor’s first call. Once you qualify, you unlock an AI simulation based on that specific investor’s thesis, criteria, and questions. 5. Meet. Pass the simulation and book directly on the investor’s calendar. Investors can also discover qualified founders and invite them first. 👉 And there’s something special for today’s launch For the next 10 days (Nov 17–27), we’re opening a Fast Track to VC funds on TheBold. Instead of pitching funds one by one, you take one AI investor-readiness interview. Pass it, and you land in the deal flow of every fund on TheBold that matches your startup, all at once. Then use your 3 meeting requests on your strongest matches. Pass the AI screening interview → Get auto-added to matching investors’ pipelines → Pick who you want to meet. Fast Track closes Nov 27. I’ll be here all day answering questions today 💬

products.name: Saparo
products.tagline: Muse for shopping with deals stacks
products.description: Saparo is a personal shopping agent that stacks every deal. Tell it what you want, and it searches U.S. stores for the same item in your size, combining promo codes, cash back, and eligible card offers that work together. It ranks options by estimated total cost, including shipping and tax, so you skip the legwork. With your approval, Saparo applies selected offers and gets checkout ready. You review the order and make the final payment yourself.
maker_comments: Hey Product Hunt 👋 I'm Silicon, COO at Saparo. I've spent my career taking products from zero to real traction. At Saparo, I work on growth and partnerships, and I spend a lot of time talking with our shoppers. Svin told you why we built Saparo, and Anson explained how it works. I want to share what we learned from the people who used it first. What early shoppers taught us: - "Just help me understand what I'll pay." People didn't want a dozen coupon codes. They wanted to see what they'd expect to pay at checkout and what they could get back later, with shipping and estimated tax clearly accounted for. So we make that breakdown easy to review. - "Don't buy anything without asking me." That's why Saparo gets checkout ready only after you give it the go-ahead. You review the order and make the final payment yourself. - "If someone found it cheaper, why didn't I?" When a shopper flags a price as too high, Saparo keeps digging, and the next person starts from the better deal. We share prices and codes, never your personal data. A few things we hold ourselves to: - Make the estimated savings clear, including when cash back or savings from eligible card offers arrive later rather than at checkout. - Remember your sizes, cards, and preferences to make shopping more useful for you. - Read every piece of feedback. A lot of what's in Saparo today started as a message from a user. 🎁 A little extra for the PH community Sign up through the link below during our launch and get 600 welcome credits—double the usual 300. Use them to try Saparo on something you're shopping for. 👉 Get your 600 welcome credits and try Saparo One honest ask 🙏 Saparo is still early, and it isn't perfect yet. If it didn't find the exact item you wanted, or a deal didn't stack the way it should, please send the details to support@saparo.ai . I'll work through it with you directly. Your feedback really does help us make Saparo better for the next shopper. And if Saparo helped you save, we'd love to hear what you bought in the comments 😄 Thanks for checking us out. I'll be here all day ❤️

products.name: Yoroll
products.tagline: Build playable stories without a game engine
products.description: Yoroll lets anyone turn stories into playable, cinematic games without coding or a game engine. Start with a script, image, or video clip, then direct the scenes, add player choices, and create branching storylines with different outcomes. AI helps bring everything together into an interactive experience you can share. It's more like directing your own interactive movie than programming a game.
maker_comments: Yoroll is doing something pretty interesting with AI video. Instead of generating clips that people just watch, it lets you turn them into interactive games with choices, different endings, and playable moments. You can start with a prompt, image, or video, then build and publish the experience without a traditional game engine. They've already got a playable version of The Odyssey with 140+ AI-generated scenes and 11 endings. Worth trying if you've ever wanted to turn a story into a game.

Hi guys! 👋 We are the LinearGame team, and we’re launching Yoroll on Product Hunt today. When we showed Yoroll at GDC and NVIDIA GTC, we kept hearing some version of “I’ve always wanted to make a game, but I never knew how to start.” That stuck with us. If you write short dramas or make AI videos, you might already know exactly where you’d let the audience take the story in a different direction. Getting that one choice to work on screen is where things get fiddly. We built Yoroll so you can start with whatever you’ve got. Got a story in mind? Bring a premise, a script, or a few reference images into Yoroll Agent. You can work out where each choice leads, review the storyboard, and pick which shots to turn into video. Then play it through and see how the story feels from the other side of the screen. Open Yoroll Agent Got a game idea? With Yoroll Code, you can build a standalone mini-game or a playable moment inside a story. Say the player has to pick a lock before a guard comes back. Try it in your browser, tweak the timer, and play it again. You’ve got Tripo 3D, Seedance video, sound effects, and the game engine in the same workspace. Try Yoroll Code Already shot a short drama? Say your lead signs a deal in the original cut. What if the audience could make her walk away? Keep the footage you shot, generate the walkout scene, and choose where that path rejoins the original story. Try the interactive drama tool For Black Friday, members can save up to 60% on Claude Fable 5.2 in Yoroll Code！ Thanks for giving Yoroll a look. If you try it, we’d love to hear what felt good, what got in your way, or what you wish it could do. And if you just want to talk about the product or kick around an idea you’re working on, we’re here for that too. 🙌

products.name: Verse Engine by Ctruh
products.tagline: Blender, Unity or Unreal to a live 3D link in one click
products.description: Verse Engine by Ctruh is a browser-native 3D and XR engine that turns any 3D into one link. Bring files, scans and floor plans, or publish straight from Blender, Unity and Unreal. The link opens in any browser with no app and no download. Built for developers, 3D artists, game studios, architects, real estate teams and e-commerce brands. A scene streams only what the viewer sees, so a 10.3 billion triangle city opens from a link on a laptop. Embeds, API and SDK included. Free 14-day Pro trial.
maker_comments: Hey Product Hunt @product I'm excited to introduce Verse Engine by Ctruh, something our team has been working hard to bring to life.One challenge we've consistently seen with 3D is that creating an experience is only part of the problem. Sharing it, making it accessible, and getting it to run smoothly in a browser can be just as challenging. Large files, software dependencies and deployment complexity often get in the way.That's what we're working to simplify with Verse Engine. Verse Engine by Ctruh is a browser-native 3D and XR engine that brings 3D content from creation to deployment. You can bring supported 3D files, scans, floor plans and projects from tools like Blender, Unity and Unreal Engine, and turn them into interactive browser experiences that can be shared through a link. No separate application installation is required for viewers. One of the demonstrations we're particularly excited about is our Lyon City experience, built around a scene with approximately 10.3 billion triangles and a 556 GB source file, explored through the browser. We're building Verse Engine towards a larger vision: making 3D and XR experiences easier to create, stream and deploy across the web. I'd love for you to try it: https://verse.ctruh.com If you're a 3D artist, developer, architect, game developer or someone working with large 3D environments, we'd love to hear your feedback. A few things we'd especially like to learn from the community: How do you currently share and deploy large 3D experiences? What is the biggest bottleneck in your 3D workflow? What would you like to see us build next?We're here to listen, learn and keep improving. Thanks for checking out Verse Engine! Best, Somesh
products.website_text: What is Verse? Verse by Ctruh is the streaming layer for 3D. You upload a 3D file, send a floor plan, or publish from Blender, Unity or Unreal, and get a link that opens in the browser with nothing to install. Video to walkthrough is in private beta, by invitation. Do viewers need an app or a plug-in? No. A Verse link opens in the browser. Viewers never pay: every published scene opens for everyone. Which tools can publish to Verse? Plug-ins for Blender, Unity and Unreal (on Mac and Windows) publish a scene with one button, and Substance 3D Painter, Revit, SketchUp and Rhino are in beta. Plug-ins for 3ds Max, Archicad, Maya, Cinema 4D, Houdini, SolidWorks, Figma and Spline are coming soon, and a BIM model arrives through IFC today. You can also upload a 3D file in the app or use the API. Is Verse free? Yes. The Free plan lets you try Verse on your own models, and a trial with Pro features starts with a creator code or a card. Starter, Pro, Scale and Enterprise add storage, bandwidth, Verse Homes, films and seats; see the pricing page. Can viewers see a product in AR? Yes, for product-sized scenes. On a handheld device, View in AR places the product in the room from its link. On a desktop, a QR code opens it on your device. How View in AR works What if an upload has a problem? Verse watches every upload. If a step fails it retries and recovers on its own, and a bad file gets a plain explanation of what to change. How is it different from a 3D library? A library gives you parts to assemble: loading, streaming, compression, hosting, sharing and analytics are yours to build. Verse ships those as one product, so a scene goes from file to link without a build project.

But doing Reddit well is a full time job. Every subreddit has its own rules, new accounts get removed, and one lazy promo comment can get you banned. So I built Rankhog to do the boring parts for me: Radar watches the subreddits your buyers hang out in and finds people asking for what you sell, while the post is still fresh. Run all of it from Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or any MCP client. What it is not: a spam bot. No mass comments, no bought accounts, no posting where the rules say no. You can start with a free Reddit audit of your product, and there are free tools too (shadowban checker, post checker, best time to post). The plan is $99 a month per product with a 7 day free trial. I would love to hear it straight: what has Reddit done for your product so far, good or bad? I'm here all day to answer.

products.name: Bluedot Phone Calls
products.tagline: AI note taker for phone calls
products.description: Bluedot now covers phone calls, not just meetings. Dial from the web or mobile app, keep your own caller ID, and get a transcript, summary and action items automatically.
maker_comments: Hey Product Hunt! Dima here, co-founder of Bluedot. Bluedot started as a note taker for online meetings that records without a bot joining the call. Then we added in-person meetings. That left one obvious gap: phone calls. A lot of real work still happens there (a follow-up with a client, a candidate screen, a quick check-in with a supplier), and those are the conversations nobody writes down. So we built phone call recording into Bluedot: Verify your number once, then call from Bluedot on web or mobile The call is recorded and transcribed, and you get a summary and action items when you hang up Call notes sit in the same workspace as your meeting notes An optional announcement tells the other person the call is being recorded Two honest limits: it’s outbound calls only for now, and we’re still adding countries. I’d love your feedback on: Would you use inbound call recording, and how would you expect it to work? Which countries should we add next? What do you do with call notes afterwards: CRM, follow-up email, something else? I’ll be here all day answering questions. Thanks for checking it out!
Really excited to see phone calls finally added. This closes a pretty obvious gap for teams that already use Bluedot for meetings. Check it out and let us know if you have any questions!
